question.problem:
The rate of growth in the frog population $P(t)$ in a certain lake follows the logistic growth model

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=0.1P(5\,000-P),
$$

where $t$ is the time, in years. Find an expression for the frog population after $t$ years, given that there were $100$ frogs initially.
question.worked_solution:
A logistic growth equation has the form

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=kP(a-P),
$$

where $k>0$ is a constant of proportionality, and $a>P$ is the carrying capacity.

The general solution to the logistic growth equation is

$$
P(t)=\frac{a}{1+C{e}^{-akt}}.
$$

In this case, the constant of proportionality is $k=0.1,$ and the carrying capacity is $a=5\,000.$ 

Therefore, the general solution to our equation is

$$
P(t)=\frac{5\,000}{1+C{e}^{-(5\,000\cdot 0.1)t}}=\frac{5\,000}{1+C{e}^{-500t}}.
$$

We now substitute the initial condition $P(0)=100$ and solve for $C.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5\,000}{1+C{e}^{-500\cdot 0}} & =100 \\ 1+C & =\frac{5\,000}{100} \\ C & =50-1 \\  & =49.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
P(t)=\frac{5\,000}{1+49{e}^{-500t}}.
$$
